correctness.rationale: Differentiating the analytic logarithm gives J_M=1-8(M-1)Re[z/(1-z^4)]/pi. The positive region is in the right half disk. H'(z)=(1+3z^4)/(1-z^4)^2 has exactly two right-half critical points z=3^(-1/4)exp(±i*pi/4), both at k*=3^(3/4)/(4sqrt(2)); H'' is nonzero. The rays arg(z)=±pi/4 have U<=k*, thus separate three pole-associated superlevel tongues at and above k*. The explicit unit-circle values 1/(4cos(theta)) and maximum principle preclude further bounded components. Below k*, the radius-3^(-1/4) arc, real radial segment and ±pi/3 radial collars connect all three tongues, and the boundary analysis excludes extra components. The strict inequality makes equality a three-component case. Independent exact factorization and radial derivative checks corroborate the key formulas; finite sampling cannot prove global connectivity.

final_claim: On the open unit disk, the negative-Jacobian set for the specified harmonic shear F_M has exactly three components for 1<M<=1+pi*sqrt(2)/(2*3^(3/4)) and one component above this threshold; at equality two nondegenerate interior harmonic saddles share the critical level.
limitations: Specific one-parameter shear, open disk and strict J<0; no full caustic or arbitrary-target valence theorem.
